text: I didn't make this payment to GadgetHub. I was asleep at 3am and I've never shopped there.
label_notes: Obvious fraud: 3am, Romania, unknown device, failed 3-D Secure, no history with merchant.

text: I cancelled StreamMax last month but they charged me again.
label_notes: Merchant dispute. Tom's past lost fraud claims don't matter: this isn't a fraud claim.

text: I paid for a sofa three weeks ago and it never arrived. The shop won't answer my calls and I'm really struggling.
label_notes: Non-delivery. 'Really struggling' plus vulnerable profile = medium, normal flow with a human.

text: This PixelGames charge isn't me, I never bought anything.
label_notes: 3 signals: earlier purchase at merchant, known device + 3-D Secure, 2 lost fraud claims.

text: My wallet was stolen on Saturday afternoon in central London and someone used my card at a watch shop. I reported it to the police.
label_notes: Obvious card-present fraud: stolen card, in-person, no history, police report.

text: I don't recognise this payment to PAYPAL *DIGIMARKT. What is it?
label_notes: Subtle: customer only says 'don't recognise'. Evidence (Germany, unknown device, failed 3-D Secure, late night) points to fraud.

text: RailGo took the money for my train ticket twice on the same morning.
label_notes: Duplicate: TX-5010 and TX-5011 same merchant, amount and minute.

text: Bella Cucina charged me £148 but our bill was £48. I think they added an extra 1 by mistake.
label_notes: Wrong amount: customer gives the correct bill amount.

text: I never ordered from FoodDash on the 20th, this isn't mine.
label_notes: 2 signals: two earlier FoodDash orders, known device + 3-D Secure. No past disputes, so letter must not accuse.

text: I'm 82 and I don't really understand online payments, my grandson set it up for me. A man phoned saying my computer was broken and now there's £299 from TechSupport Pro. I didn't agree to that.
label_notes: Likely scam. Profile not marked vulnerable: the text alone must trigger the flag (age, low digital capability).

text: Someone took £600 from my account last night and now I can't pay my rent. I can't cope with any of this anymore and I don't see the point in anything.
label_notes: HIGH risk: possible crisis language. Must go straight to a human. No AI recommendation expected.

text: I'm absolutely furious! I cancelled StreamMax in October and they've charged me AGAIN. Sort this out.
label_notes: Tricky: anger is NOT vulnerability. Level must be none.

text: Something's wrong with my statement, there's a payment on there I don't understand.
label_notes: VAGUE. Unfamiliar billing name, but customer bought from the same marketplace in October on her own device with 3-D Secure. Likely her own purchase.

text: I want my money back for the FlyHigh charge. I never got to use it.
label_notes: VAGUE. 'Never got to use it' = service not provided.

text: Can you look at the £45 from GymPlus? I thought I'd stopped that.
label_notes: VAGUE and hedged ('I thought'). Monthly repeat charge = cancelled recurring.

text: My blender from KitchenPro arrived smashed, and on top of that I think they charged me twice.
label_notes: MIXED. Trap: duplicate_charge. The data shows only ONE KitchenPro payment, so the real problem is damaged goods.

text: StyleLane's delivery was three days late, which was annoying, but the real problem is they charged me £120 when the jacket was £100.
label_notes: MIXED. Trap: goods_not_received. It did arrive (late); the dispute is the amount.

text: I cancelled MealBox ages ago, and now there's a £54 charge from them at 4am that I definitely didn't make.
label_notes: MIXED. Trap: cancelled_recurring. 4am from the Netherlands, unknown device, failed 3-D Secure = fraud.

text: There's a £149.99 GameVault payment from the middle of the night. That wasn't me.
label_notes: LOOKALIKE: real fraud that looks like friendly fraud. Earlier GameVault purchase + 1 lost claim trip the friendly-fraud rule, but unknown device in Brazil with failed 3-D Secure says fraud. Current triage gets this WRONG on purpose.

text: Someone has used my card at ToyWorld! I never shop there.
label_notes: LOOKALIKE: sounds like fraud, but an earlier ToyWorld order exists, on her own device with 3-D Secure. Possibly a child in the household. Never accuse.

text: Money's a bit tight this month so I really need this £60 back. QuickFix Repairs never turned up.
label_notes: LOW: mild money worry. Normal flow, flagged.

text: I've just moved house and I'm still sorting everything out, but I don't think I ordered this from HomeBits.
label_notes: LOW: house move. Earlier HomeBits order on her own device: likely forgotten purchase. Gentle letter.

text: Sorry if this is confusing, I've got a new baby and haven't slept. I think BabyCo charged me twice for the pram.
label_notes: LOW: new parent. Two identical BabyCo payments at the same minute.

text: This is a bloody joke. Third time I've had to write in. PhoneHub charged me £95 when the price was £59.
label_notes: TRAP: strong language and frustration are NOT vulnerability. Level none.

text: After everything this year I feel like there's no way out. Now £400 has gone to something called LuxeStay and I just can't face dealing with it.
label_notes: HIGH, SUBTLE: no explicit self-harm words, but 'no way out' + 'can't face it' is crisis language. Must go straight to a human.
